# How to Market Your Local App - The Most Useful Guide

After investing in the creation of a local app, getting it found is a high priority. The mobile market is becoming increasingly dominant with app usage…

By Robert Kazmi · 7 min read

![](/blog/marketing-local-app/NO-TEXT_Marketing-Your-Local-App_hu_6c792d1df10a0ae8.webp)

[Building an app](https://www.koombea.com/blog/app-development-cost/) for your local business, or building local content into your app makes a lot of sense for many businesses. Why? The mobile market is becoming increasingly dominant with app usage having grown 90% since 2013 according to [Comscore](https://www.comscore.com/Insights/Presentations-and-Whitepapers/2015/The-2015-US-Mobile-App-Report).

Understanding how local mobile apps are developing along with increasing mobile use is key. It makes sense: you need locally based content so mobile users can find it when they’re nearby. Savvy companies are using new technology to find, contact, and deliver an experience to local users like never before.

One of the big challenges for creators of local apps is not just getting them found, but getting them found by the local audience they are targeted at. There is a lot of “noise” in the app space and you’re competing in the clamour for attention with the big names.

What can you be doing to market your local app?

## Android Nearby

One of the hot new developments of the Android space has been the recent announcement of their new [“Nearby” feature](https://android.googleblog.com/2016/06/introducing-nearby-new-way-to-discover.html). For developers of Android apps, this is a great tool to keep in mind when you’re considering how you will market your local app.

The Nearby feature works by notifying Android users of things that may be useful to them nearby, including local apps. For example, if you are near the [University of Notre Dame](https://www.nd.edu/) you might be invited to tour historic landmarks, if you are at [The Broad](https://web.archive.org/web/20180309193321/https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=nz.co.stqry.thebroadapp) in LA, you might be invited to download their app and take an audio tour.

These proximity-based experiences are another way of offering more relevant content to an audience that wants it, with “user choice” being the key here. Just because someone is nearby with an Android phone doesn’t necessarily mean they will be notified of your app. Users have the choice to opt in to receiving these notifications by turning on Bluetooth and Location. If they’ve opted in and receive notifications they are not interested in, they simply swipe them away.

### How does this work for your app?

If you’ve got a local Android app, you need to have set it up so that you’re able to take advantage of Nearby. [Google’s developer blog](https://developers.googleblog.com/2016/06/surface-new-proximity-based-experiences.html) has the details; basically, you will need to invest in some Eddystone Beacons which you then configure to point to your desired experience.

Obviously, this is a great initiative for local app developers wanting to draw more attention to their Android app and could provide quick wins by taking advantage of technology. However, given that receiving notifications or having location enabled at all is optional, you’ll need some other ways to [market your app](https://www.koombea.com/blog/data-driven-marketing-optimize-engagement/) to a local audience too.

## App Indexing

App indexing is not so much about marketing, but getting your app found in searches — like SEO, except for apps. Why does this really matter for local apps? Research from Think With Google tells us that one in four app users discovers an app through search, while discovery via search is particularly prominent for local apps.

![App Indexing](/blog/marketing-local-app/google-app-search_hu_f208165fc7d58c82.webp)

First up, here’s a “watch this space” for app indexing which you should be aware of.

Google began testing several months ago on indexing app-only content according to [Search Engine Land](http://searchengineland.com/google-expands-app-indexing-to-find-stream-content-only-within-apps-236288). What this means is that if someone were to search, say for a nearby Thai restaurant, Google might show them in-app content results, even if there is no corresponding website content.

There are a few catches at the moment: if users are searching in Chrome, they will only see the app-only content results for those apps which they have already downloaded. If they are using the Google search app, they will see in-app content results as Google is testing out “streaming” of apps — where people can jump to the app content even if they haven’t got the app downloaded.

Other catches are that the apps involved are only a select group at present (Hotel Tonight and Weather Channel are among them) and it is only Android apps and for searches on Android phones. This could, of course, be expanded in the future for iOS and for more apps if their testing goes well.

Other app platforms are not to be left out — look out for [Apple App Search](https://web.archive.org/web/20210812214328/https://searchengineland.com/library/apple-2/apple-app-search-deep-linking) (which was actually around first) and which allows developers to feed information into Spotlight and Safari search results.

[Facebook’s AppLinks](http://applinks.org/) is another platform to be aware of when looking at getting your app found in search. This allows “deep linking” from app to app in the same way that web pages can link together.

In every case, you need to be set up to allow the links, so check the requirements on their pages.

### Getting found on Google

Most of us can rule out getting found for app-only content until this is rolled out further, but keep an eye on developments so you can get in if and when it becomes available. In the meantime, you need to have app content associated with a web page to be indexed. Here’s how you can still ensure you appear in Google results:

*   You need to correctly implement “deep linking” for apps which have corresponding web content. For example, the app for your local cafe may be linked to the company website. (If your app is for iOS, you need to support [Universal Links](https://developer.apple.com/library/ios/documentation/General/Conceptual/AppSearch/UniversalLinks.html). Android apps need to be registered with Google and associated with your website).
*   You need to implement Google App Indexing. For iOS, you need to integrate [App Indexing SDK](https://firebase.google.com/docs/app-indexing/ios/app), for Android use the [App Indexing API for

# Small But Mighty: How to Use Apps to Improve Your Marketing

From social media time savers to simple ways to automate marketing tasks, digital tools help solopreneurs and small teams do a lot with a little.

BY [INC. CUSTOM STUDIO](https://www.inc.com/author/inc-custom-studio)

May 23, 2019

SHARE

![SockFancy](https://img-cdn.inc.com/image/upload/f_webp,c_fit,w_1920,q_auto/images/panoramic/1_SlzX9QlbHMfjTb5xU_huVQ_393400.jpeg)

Digital [marketing](https://www.inc.com/marketing "Marketing") lets you connect with your audience any time in a personalized way. But, with all of that promotional opportunity just a few clicks away, you may feel overwhelmed. As a small business owner, the more you can organize, automate, and streamline marketing tasks, the more successful you will be.

Fortunately, there are a number of digital tools that can help you tackle key marketing areas. These apps are proven game-changers for entrepreneurs who use those tactics, and they can help you improve and simplify the following aspects of digital marketing.

_Social media management_

[Stringjoy](https://www.stringjoy.com/), a boutique guitar string company based in Nashville, Tennessee, uses Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, and YouTube to build personal, long-lasting relationships with its customers. Founder and President Scott Marquart says monitoring interactions on multiple social accounts gets “wily and unwieldy pretty quickly.” He recommends [Agorapulse](https://www.agorapulse.com/), a social media management tool that filters social mentions and messages into one inbox. Pricing starts at $79 per month.

“Customers will communicate on whatever platform they are most comfortable with. If their order doesn’t arrive, they might drop a comment on your YouTube video or Instagram post. Having an app that integrates everything is essential, so you don’t miss opportunities,” Marquart says.

In 2015, Marquart did Instagram hashtag research to see what posts were resonating with guitar lovers. He started applying Stringjoy strings to cool-looking guitars and sharing the photos on his feed. The company still uses this strategy today, using [Later](https://later.com/), a mobile app for planning and scheduling Instagram posts. Later has a free version for individuals and a $19-per-month plan for small businesses. [Buffer](https://buffer.com/) is a popular multi-platform management choice. Costs range from $16-$99 per month for small businesses.

_Digital graphics customization_

Apps and tools can also simplify graphic design, allowing you to create social media ads, landing pages, and other marketing material. Amy Birks, a digital marketing strategist and author of _The_ _Hustle-Free Business_, recommends [Word Swag](http://wordswag.co/), an app for creating custom text designs to add to photos. Her other favorite app for small businesses is [Canva](https://www.canva.com/), a graphic design tool that makes it simple to create professional-looking content. Both apps are free to use and offer additional features for purchase.

Stefan Lewinger, founder and CEO of [Sock Fancy](https://sockfancy.com/), an online monthly sock subscription service, works hard to “create a customer experience worth sharing.” The company uses Mailchimp, a multifaceted small business marketing platform, to find and build relationships with its customers. The [Mailchimp ad builder](https://mailchimp.com/features/facebook-ads/) lets you build professional Facebook and Instagram ads and use audience segment tools for better targeting. Mailchimp’s template library also lets business owners design effective landing pages, and flexible pricing scales with your business.

_Sales integration_

You can’t sell online without a point of sale (POS) or e-commerce platform. Popular choices like Square and WooCommerce have apps so you can manage your business on the go and complete in-person transactions, too.

When building your marketing technology stack, look for tools that “play well with others.” [Mailchimp’s customer relationship managemen](https://mailchimp.com/features/crm/)[t](http://mailchimp.com/features/crm/) (CRM) function integrates with leading e-commerce platforms, as well as Salesforce. This allows you to use all the data at your disposal to make smart marketing decisions.

# How a Mobile App Can Help Your Small Business

*   July 24, 2020
*   Rosie's Creative LLC
*   [Marketing](https://rosiescreative.com/category/marketing/), [Rosie's Creative](https://rosiescreative.com/category/rosies-creative/)

![](https://rosiescreative.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Rosies-Creative_Mobile-Apps_SM.jpg)

**The World at Your Fingertips**

In 2016, tech observers and marketing pros alike took notice when mobile internet use surpassed desktop for the first time **[– and four years on, there’s no looking back.](https://techcrunch.com/2016/11/01/mobile-internet-use-passes-desktop-for-the-first-time-study-finds/)** Today, majorities of U.S. consumers across every demographic use some kind of mobile device to access the internet, and for small businesses today, a robust, multi-faceted strategy to reach mobile users is crucial to long-term success.

**[From mobile-friendly and responsive web design](https://rosiescreative.com/2019/09/25/mobile-friendly-vs-responsive-design-whats-the-difference/)**, to social media, text messaging, **[email marketing](https://rosiescreative.com/2020/06/22/the-power-of-email-marketing/)** and more, digital marketers employ a range of methods to help brands connect with today’s mobile-connected consumers. And now, more small businesses are turning to a new tool to get an edge over the competition – custom-built mobile apps.

Now, you may think a custom-built app is something only big businesses can afford – and in years past, this was indeed the case. But today, new tools have dramatically lowered the cost of developing simple, effective custom apps, bringing the price point to a more reasonable level. And small businesses are taking advantage, **[with a 2018 survey finding that 42% already have a mobile app](https://clutch.co/app-developers/resources/small-business-apps-survey-2018)**, with another 30% looking to develop one in the future.

Let’s look at a few of the top reasons to consider a mobile app for your small business…

**Tackle tough problems with focused design**  
Because apps are built with a specific goal or target in mind, they’re a terrific way to zero in on a precise pain point or resolve a nagging problem. So, if you’re looking for a targeted fix to improve your customers’ experience or help your business operate more efficiently, a custom-tailored app could be just the solution.

**Build brand loyalty by offering convenience**  
With the often-hectic pace of modern life, the convenience factor is a big-time selling point for consumers, and in the post-COVID world this is truer than ever. When a user downloads your app to their device, suddenly, your brand is in their pocket and at their fingertips, anytime and anywhere – making apps a great way to build brand loyalty and boost brand awareness.

**Use data to learn what makes your customers tick**  
Understanding your customer base is key to success for businesses of any size. And, alongside other top digital tools, an app can help to bolster that understanding by collecting useful data that can help you fine-tune your marketing efforts and engage with customers more effectively.

**Boost your business with apps for internal use**  
Finally, apps aren’t just for the end user – mobile apps for internal use can be just as vital to the success of your business, helping you coordinate, communicate, and run a more efficient and effective operation. Use custom business management apps to share files, monitor inventory, manage workflow, and much more.

**With a custom-built mobile app, your brand can project an image of sleek, modern professionalism – and your business can get a much-needed boost in today’s competitive marketplace.** So, if you’re considering the advantages of developing a mobile app for your business, contact us at Rosie’s Creative today, and let’s get started.  _**[Your first consultation is always free!](https://rosiescreative.com/contact)**_
